newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper to continue retreat from $2,600.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper to continue retreat from $2,600.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper prices are seen continuing a retracement from last Thursday's levels above $2,600, with the market unwinding overbought indicators, analysts said.
Aluminium may have to follow, especially if prices are hit by pricing sales against "third Wednesday" later on Monday, and $1,570/75 may come under pressure, they said.
Prices had fallen back since last Thursday, but an RSI at 77 percent was still close to the overbought level, leaving scope for further technical adjustment, analysts added.

"The market is looking to consolidate around the $2,570/80 level...A chart gap between $2,514 and $2,532.50 is now evident and this may need to be filled before prices can sustain another upwards thrust," LME trader Brandeis said.
Analyst Harry Creates of Amalgamated Metal Trading said $2,570 was very important support, and if that level was broken then the market could head towards $2,520.

On the fundamental side the labour stoppage at Inco Sudbury and concentrate shipment delays in Papua New Guineau remained in play. Heavy rains in Chile did not appear to have hit production, traders noted.
At 0843 three months LME copper was quoted at $2,565/70, down from Friday's late close of $2,570/73.
Prices were holding close to pre-weekend levels, but the market's recent weak performances, despite strong copper, suggested the downside would remain under pressure, traders said.
"It has broken through support around $1,600 and closed poorly on the chart. A test of $1,575 looks likely which would indicate a correction back to $1,540," Brandeis said.
The $1,600 level also represented the 10-day moving average -- that was broken on Friday -- while there was also a well-defined triple-top formation, LME trader Gerald noted.
At 0843 three months aluminium was quoted at $1,579/81, little changed from the previous late close.
